title: Halloumi with honeyed turnips and kale

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Halloumi, tinned chickpeas, honey, kale and turnips are all plain whole foods with no jars, stock pots or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: Every item is a mainstream Tesco staple, and two packs of halloumi are an everyday price for a family dinner.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan and a saucepan, and the techniques are basic frying and wilting.

works.reason: The amounts suit four (500g turnips, two tins of chickpeas, 200g kale, 450g halloumi), the timings are sensible, and halloumi fries happily in a dry wiped pan.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is believable for wedging the turnips, slicing the onion, garlic and halloumi and shredding the kale, and the cook time roughly matches 15 minutes of frying plus batch-fried halloumi, though it runs a few minutes over.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot pan supper suits early January, and the honey-glazed turnips are a main component rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain British English instructions that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Chickpeas, kale, turnips and halloumi make a filling, balanced vegetarian dinner that a family would want again.
